claims.text: Short-duration, low-temperature post-solidification annealing can simultaneously improve room-temperature tensile strength and ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The proposed annealing improvement operates by healing and strengthening internal lamellar boundaries.
As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 has a fine lamellar FCC/B2 dual-phase microstructure.
The fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 microstructure contains numerous internal inter-lamellar boundaries.
Internal lamellar boundaries in the as-cast alloy act as microcrack-nucleation sites.
A subcritical annealing temperature can promote limited interfacial diffusion.
Keeping annealing temperature and duration sufficiently low can prevent lamellar coarsening while allowing boundary healing.
Mild interfacial diffusion and healing enhance cohesion at internal lamellar boundaries.
Limited diffusion at dual-phase interfaces heals weak spots and reduces microcrack initiation during loading.
Reinforced lamellar interfaces enhance load transfer during deformation.
Enhanced interfacial load transfer concurrently increases tensile strength and ductility relative to an untreated as-cast baseline.
Annealed specimens will exhibit statistically significant improvements in room-temperature tensile strength and ductility.
Annealed specimens will exhibit fewer and less severe microcracks originating at lamellar boundaries.
The unmodified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic alloy has high room-temperature strength.
The unmodified eutectic alloy has limited room-temperature ductility.
The unmodified alloy fails brittly because cracks initiate at weak internal boundaries.
Excessive annealing temperature or time can destabilize or coarsen the fine lamellar structure.
The beneficial effect is restricted to annealing conditions that alter interfacial bonding without changing overall lamellar morphology.

contradictions.description: The baseline characterizes the as-cast eutectic alloy as having limited ductility and brittle failure, whereas the cited AlCoCrFeNi2.1 abstract reports an unprecedented combination of high room-temperature tensile ductility and high fracture strength.
